titleZh: 在城市的一角，种下一座花园

cet4.title: A Little Garden, a Bigger Community
cet4.summary: 周六早晨，人们带着植物、旧水桶和工具来到社区里一块曾经堆积垃圾的空地，把它变成共享花园。它并非要养活整座城市，而是让居民有机会共同劳动，关注身边的环境。

paragraphs.text: On Saturday mornings, an empty corner of a busy neighbourhood begins to change. People arrive with small plants, old buckets and a few simple tools. The land once collected rubbish. Now it is becoming a community garden. Nobody expects it to feed the whole city. Its value lies in something smaller: giving local people a reason to work together and notice the place where they live.
paragraphs.translation: 周六早晨，人们带着植物、旧水桶和工具来到社区里一块曾经堆积垃圾的空地，把它变成共享花园。它并非要养活整座城市，而是让居民有机会共同劳动，关注身边的环境。

paragraphs.text: Growing food also makes everyday choices easier to understand. A tomato does not appear overnight. Someone must prepare the soil, water the plant and protect it from damage. When children take part, they see the effort behind an ordinary meal. Adults learn too. A dry week can start a conversation about saving water, while fallen leaves can become useful material instead of waste.
paragraphs.translation: 亲手种菜让人理解日常选择：番茄需要整地、浇水和保护，孩子能看到一顿普通饭菜背后的劳动。成年人也能从干旱和落叶中学习节水与资源利用。

paragraphs.text: However, a shared garden needs more than enthusiasm. Volunteers must agree on who waters the plants and how the harvest is shared. Some people can visit only at weekends. Others cannot do heavy work. Clear arrangements allow each person to contribute in a suitable way. A noticeboard with a weekly schedule may be less exciting than planting, but it can prevent many misunderstandings.
paragraphs.translation: 共享花园不仅需要热情，还需要分工和收获分配的约定。不同居民的时间与体力不同，清晰、灵活的安排让每个人都能作出合适的贡献，周计划能减少误会。

paragraphs.text: The garden succeeds when it remains open to different people. A retired neighbour might teach a student to grow beans. A new family might bring seeds from home and explain how to cook the vegetables. Not every plant will survive, and not everyone will become a skilled gardener. Yet a patch of land can still produce an important result: neighbours who recognise, trust and help one another.
paragraphs.translation: 花园应向不同的人开放。邻居可以交流种植与烹饪经验。即使植物未能全部成活、人人未必成为园艺高手，这块土地仍能培养邻里间的认识、信任与互助。

paragraphs.text: A beginner can start with one manageable job, such as watering a small bed. Taking responsibility for that job makes progress visible. It also creates a chance to ask an experienced neighbour for advice. Small successes give people a reason to return, even when a larger project would initially feel difficult.
paragraphs.translation: 新手可以先承担给一小块地浇水的明确任务，向有经验的邻居请教，在可见的小进步中建立责任感与继续参与的动力。

questions.prompt: What is the main value of the garden described in the passage?
options: It gives neighbours an opportunity to work together.
It replaces all the food shops in the city.
It guarantees a profit for every resident.
It requires everyone to become a professional gardener.
questions.explanation: 文章强调共同参与及邻里关系，而不是产量或利润。

questions.prompt: Why is growing a tomato a useful learning experience?
options: It proves that plants never need protection.
It removes the need to save water.
It makes every crop grow overnight.
It reveals the resources and effort behind food.
questions.explanation: 种植过程让食物背后的水、时间和劳动变得可见。

questions.prompt: What helps volunteers with different abilities participate?
options: Allowing only people who can visit every day.
Avoiding discussion about responsibilities.
Offering flexible arrangements and different tasks.
Asking everyone to carry the same heavy tools.
questions.explanation: 灵活分工能让不同时间与体力条件的人参与。

questions.prompt: Which problem could unclear arrangements cause?
options: An automatic improvement in the soil.
Disagreements about duties and sharing.
A guaranteed increase in food supply.
The disappearance of every plant disease.
questions.explanation: 缺少明确安排容易引发分工与分配方面的争议。

questions.prompt: What is the author’s overall attitude?
options: Supportive, while recognising practical limits.
Certain that gardens solve every city problem.
Opposed to all shared outdoor spaces.
Interested only in the price of vegetables.
questions.explanation: 作者肯定花园的价值，同时承认其效果受组织和现实条件限制。

cet6.title: Urban Gardens: Growing More Than Food
cet6.summary: 周六早晨，人们带着植物、旧水桶和工具来到社区里一块曾经堆积垃圾的空地，把它变成共享花园。它并非要养活整座城市，而是让居民有机会共同劳动，关注身边的环境。

paragraphs.text: A community garden may occupy only a neglected corner of a city, yet its significance extends beyond the vegetables it produces. By transforming an unused plot into a shared space, residents gain an opportunity to influence their immediate environment. The attraction is not necessarily economic efficiency. Buying a tomato may be cheaper than growing one. What the garden offers is participation: a visible connection between individual effort and a collective outcome.
paragraphs.translation: 社区花园的价值超越蔬菜产量：居民把闲置地变为共享空间，也获得影响周边环境的机会。它未必在经济上更划算，但能让个人努力与共同成果之间的联系变得可见。

paragraphs.text: This connection can reshape how people understand consumption. Gardening reveals the time, water and labour hidden behind familiar products. A failed crop makes uncertainty tangible, while a successful harvest demonstrates the value of patient attention. For children, these experiences can complement classroom discussions about natural systems. For adults, they may encourage a more thoughtful attitude towards food waste. Such learning is practical rather than automatic; it depends on opportunities to observe, discuss and reflect.
paragraphs.translation: 种植揭示了商品背后的时间、水与劳动。失败让不确定性具体可感，收获体现耐心的价值。这些经历可补充课堂知识、促进减少浪费，但学习仍需要观察、交流与反思。

paragraphs.text: The social benefits are equally dependent on organisation. A garden described as communal can still be dominated by the few residents with the most spare time. Without clear expectations, disputes may arise over access, responsibilities and the distribution of produce. Flexible schedules and varied tasks can reduce these barriers. Someone unable to dig could maintain records or welcome newcomers. Fair participation means recognising different contributions, rather than requiring everyone to perform an identical amount of physical work.
paragraphs.translation: 社会收益也依赖组织。空闲时间最多的人可能主导花园，因此需要清楚界定使用权、责任和收获分配。公平参与应承认记录维护、接待新人等不同形式的贡献。

paragraphs.text: Long-term access to the land is another consideration. Residents may be reluctant to invest their energy if the site could disappear without notice. Clear agreements with the landowner therefore matter as much as good soil. The garden also needs a way to resolve disagreement and introduce new volunteers. These arrangements are not obstacles to community spirit; they are part of the infrastructure that allows it to develop.
paragraphs.translation: 长期土地使用权同样重要。没有稳定预期，居民可能不愿投入。与地主的明确约定、争议解决机制和新人加入渠道，是社区合作得以持续的基础。

paragraphs.text: It would be unreasonable to present small gardens as a complete solution to urban food supply or social isolation. Their effects vary with location, resources and management. Nevertheless, judging them solely by the weight of vegetables harvested would overlook their broader purpose. A productive garden can cultivate relationships, local knowledge and a sense of shared responsibility. Its most enduring achievement may be that residents begin to see the neighbourhood as a place they can shape together.
paragraphs.translation: 小花园并不能彻底解决食物供应或孤独问题，其影响随条件而异。只以产量评价会忽略它在培养关系、地方知识和共同责任感方面的价值。

paragraphs.text: For newcomers, a clearly defined first task can provide an accessible entry into the group. Responsibility for watering a particular bed, for example, creates a visible relationship between an action and its consequences. Experienced members can offer guidance without taking the task away. This balance between support and ownership helps participation develop gradually. It also makes space for people whose confidence grows through practical experience rather than through speaking at a formal meeting.
paragraphs.translation: 清晰的入门任务让新人逐步参与。有经验者提供指导却不接管任务，能平衡支持与自主，也为更习惯通过实践而非会议发言建立信心的人创造空间。
